summary: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak in 1928, later serving there as a lecturer in Chinese (1946) and professor (1956–1975), succeeding Duyvendak.

Anthony Hendrik Nicolaas Verwey was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1937–1942) and Leiden University (~1946–1950), and served at the National Museum of Ethnology from 1947 to 1981.
Anthony J. Alston worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Hari Prasad Shastri (~1948–1956) and completed his PhD at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti (~1959–1964).

Anthony Kennedy Warder was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under William Stede and earned a doctorate under John Brough at SOAS (1949–1954). He held posts at the University of Edinburgh, Pali Text Society, and University of Toronto.

Anthony Tribe works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an undergraduate degree at the University of Bristol, studying under Paul Williams and Steven Collins, and a DPhil at the University of Oxford (1995) supervised by Alexis Sanderson.

Anthony W. Barber specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984 and was affiliated with the University of Calgary, attested in 1998.
Antoine Bazin was a sinologist who studied under Stanislas Julien at the Collège de France (~1832–1840). In 1852, he held the post of Secrétaire-adjoint at the Société Asiatique.

Antoine Cabaton worked in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and at the École du Louvre, later holding posts at the BnF, EFEO, INALCO, and the École Nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer.

Antoine Grégoire was a linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at Liège, Leipzig, Munich, and Paris under Brugmann, Sievers, Hirt, Kuhn, Bréal, Henry, and Meillet. He held professorships at the University of Liège and Université libre de Bruxelles.
Antoine Lutz completed his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the doctoral supervision of Francisco Varela.

Antoine Marie Tabard was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He taught mathematics, physics, and chemistry at St. Joseph's University (1891–1924), founded The Mythic Society in 1909, and served as its president in 1910.
Antoine Meillet was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1887–1891) and Abel Bergaigne (~1887–1888).
Antoine Mosac worked in Indology and religious studies. He served as Superior of the Jesuit Mission of Chandernagore in 1742 and as Superior of the Paris Foreign Missions Society from 1775 to 1777.
Antoine-Gaspard Bellin was an Indology scholar who earned a Dr.iuris at the University of Lyon (~1835–1839). He served as a civil judge and librarian at the Tribunal civil de Lyon.

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He held chairs in Arabic (1795) and Persian (1806) at INALCO, and served as president and Vorsitzender of the Société Asiatique between 1822 and 1834.

Antoine-Jean Saint-Martin worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Collège des Quatre-Nations and at INALCO under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at the Imprimerie Nationale, Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, and the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.
Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier worked in the field of Indology. He studied under the traditional teacher Ramchandra and served as a Colonel in the East India Company.

Antoine-Léonard Chézy, an Indology and linguistics scholar, studied at Collège de Navarre, and under Silvestre de Sacy and Langlès. He was professor of Sanskrit at Collège de France (1815–1832) and professor of Persian at INALCO (1824–1827).

Anton Boller was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Vienna in 1831. He spent his career there as a Dozent and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics from 1845 onward.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned a Dr. phil. under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin (1828–1831), later serving at the Royal Danish Library and as a Dozent at Berlin (1849–1852).
